title: New in TravStats {{version}}
subtitle: A short overview of the most important changes.

design.title: One look for web and app
design.body: TravStats now looks like the Companion app: the same colours, spacing and type, one heading per page, a dark mode that comes from the colour tokens instead of special rules. Settings are split into groups: flights, cruises and lodging each have an address of their own, while account, display, data and services are sections on the general page. The admin area is a page of its own beside them — no longer a submenu.

evidence.title: Every number shows what it is made of
evidence.body: Click a figure or a row in a ranking and a panel lists the entries that produced it — flights, cruises, stays, places — with each entry's share. What cannot be attributed is said rather than dropped: a total without an exchange rate stays empty and names the reason. The panel can be shared as a link.

yearCompare.title: The running year compares fairly
yearCompare.body: A part year used to stand against a whole one and read like a collapse in September. The running year is now compared with the same span of the previous year, and the label says so. Where a figure comes from the server per year, it honestly says “vs. the full year”. The comparison moves for everyone whose year is still running.

documents.title: Documents and receipts have a home
documents.body: Boarding passes, hotel invoices and booking confirmations now live as documents on the entry they belong to, and a receipt is attached to what it proves. TravStats reads every document it knows — a photographed invoice, a boarding pass through its barcode, a Booking.com mail through a fixed template — and files it instead of leaving it lying around.

placesPassport.title: Places and the passport are finished
placesPassport.body: Places are a full domain with lists, checklists and a CSV import that also takes a Google Takeout export; the passport shows countries with their evidence. Both sat behind the beta switch since 2.6 and are simply there now — as is the colour per domain, which has become an ordinary setting.

toursAndSummary.title: Tours, the AI summary and Dawarich are released
toursAndSummary.body: A trip can be walked, driven or cycled: tours have a tab of their own on the trip, with a route editor. The AI summary of a trip now names only what the data holds — no invented hotel, no sentence about missing days. Location history from Dawarich counts as evidence for a country.

inbox.title: Inbox with tabs, a logbook that pages, the app on your home screen
inbox.body: The inbox sorts flight updates, open questions and suggestions into tabs with status counts. The logbook shows one page instead of every row while the summary strip still counts everything. And TravStats can be installed as a web app — an icon on the home screen, without the browser frame.

beta.title: Only app pairing is still beta
beta.body: Everything that sat behind the beta switch in 2.6 is finished in 2.7 — except one thing: pairing with the TravStats Companion app. Pairing itself works; what is unfinished is the app. Its registry entry says when it comes back.

countries.title: Countries count by evidence, not by landing
countries.body: A country counts when something proves you were there: a completed stay, a recorded place, a port call, a night, a day driven through from your location history — no longer where a flight touched down. Every counted country names its evidence, how strictly is a setting (an instance default, overridable per account), and data that contradicts itself goes to the inbox instead of being corrected silently. The number moves for every account. The inbox is always in the menu now.

lodging.title: Hotels are a domain of their own
lodging.body: Stays are now kept like flights and cruises: with chain, room, board, per-category ratings, price, loyalty programme and the trip they belong to. They appear on the map as pins and count towards statistics and achievements — and switching the domain off removes it everywhere without touching your data.

documents.title: Bookings and documents are read for you, in any currency
documents.body: Booking.com mails are read by a deterministic template: measured against 95 real confirmations it finds the stay in 93 and the price in all 93 — across both layouts the sender uses. Anything it does not recognise takes the same AI path flights do. A document now announces itself: a photographed hotel bill is a document, a boarding pass is read by its barcode first, package-tour paperwork is recognised — and a marketing newsletter no longer becomes a flight. A price may be written in any currency. Conversion goes through the European Central Bank, and for the currencies it does not publish, through a free dataset you can switch off as the operator. Where no rate exists the amount stays in its own currency, is marked "no rate", counts towards no total — and the total tells you how many entries it is missing. You may enter a rate yourself; it is always shown as yours, never as an official one.

imports.title: In and out: spreadsheet and CSV
imports.body: The whole logbook exports to one spreadsheet and comes back — flights, cruises, stays. The CSV import shows what it will do first, asks about likely duplicates, and every import leaves a trace that can be taken back as a whole.

stats.title: Statistics and achievements have grown
stats.body: Records, the whole route network and the year in review come from the server, every statistics tab shows only the blocks you want, hotels have a chapter of their own, and every flight has a page to read it on. Plus 78 new achievements for places and hotels.

security.title: Two-factor and passkeys
security.body: You can protect your account with a second factor — TOTP, with single-use recovery codes — or with a passkey that replaces the password entirely. Both live in the new security section of the settings.

beta.title: The beta switch says what it turns on
beta.body: Unfinished areas sit behind a switch in the admin settings: places as a domain of their own with lists, checklists and the import of saved Google Maps lists, the passport, a colour per domain, the AI summary of a trip — and tours (a trip walked, driven, cycled, with a route editor), pairing with the TravStats Companion app and the Dawarich connection. Each entry says why it is still hidden and when it comes back. Off is the default; turn it on to test.

flightsTable.title: The flight table reads like a departures board
flightsTable.body: Every row now carries the airline as a brand tile, departure and arrival share one time column, country flags mark the route, and the actions are icons instead of text buttons. A dot on the row tells you where the data came from.

immich.title: Trip photos from your own Immich
immich.body: You can link Immich albums straight to a trip — either linked only, which keeps the images on your server and uses no storage here, or as a real import. The gallery groups by album, any picture can become the cover, and a re-sync picks up stragglers.

companions.title: Companions are real records now
companions.body: Travel companions are no longer free text on a single record. You create them once and reuse them everywhere — in flights, trips, cruises and special flights, through the same picker. Your existing entries are migrated automatically on startup.

flightForm.title: One flight form, scheduled and actual times
flightForm.body: Adding and editing finally use the same form. New: scheduled and actual times with the delay calculated for you, boarding group, trip assignment, cost and receipt — and airline and aircraft type come from the catalogue. A field you clear stays cleared instead of quietly keeping the old value.

status.title: Status follows from the dates
status.body: Whether something is planned, under way or done is now derived from its dates and refreshed hourly — for flights, cruises and trips alike. The manual status picker is gone as a result; the only state you still set yourself is "cancelled".

stats.title: Anonymous usage statistics
stats.body: TravStats can now optionally send anonymous usage data. It is off by default, and you can turn it back off at any time.

whatsNew.title: This dialog
whatsNew.body: After every update you will see a one-time summary of what changed.

colorModes.title: Map colors that listen to you
colorModes.body: Flight and cruise coloring are now proper modes: status, frequency, per journey, or a single custom color. The color picker finally works everywhere — and the legend always matches what the map actually shows.

airlines.title: Airlines by name
airlines.body: Instead of cryptic codes like "DLH" you now see "Lufthansa" — in the table, the list and the calendar. Flights that only carry an ICAO code now resolve correctly too.

map.title: The map, your way
map.body: New: flat 2D routes along the true great circle as an alternative to 3D arcs. Also: place names with special characters, consistent dot sizes for airports and ports, and direction arrows that sit right on long legs.

fixes.title: Reported bugs fixed
fixes.body: Profile picture and birthday now survive a reload, "Compare with" in statistics is remembered, and booking and ticket numbers can be entered right when adding a flight manually.

polish.title: A tidier interface
polish.body: The map menu remembers whether it was open, the year selector is readable again, buttons have better contrast — and unfinished features stay hidden by default until they are ready.
